records.claim: Three deliberately irrelevant recovery sequences preserve the final reserved turn but still reach AWAITING_APPROVAL with UNKNOWN and absent decisive evidence. Optional recovery permits success; it does not enforce evidence sufficiency.
limitations: No contradiction of H19 narrow affordance hypothesis; no proof of autonomous recovery.
Scripted adversarial policy, not a GLM behavior estimate.

records.next_action: Freeze a live model-selection comparison, keeping premature submission and irrelevant or exhausted recovery visible. Do not claim the completion gate now proves evidence sufficiency.

experiment_template.research_question: Does GLM use newly available archive recovery to resolve a masked revised fact before submission?
stop_conditions: No dispatch before exact source, fixture and call-budget binding.
No retry, replacement or hidden-oracle feedback.

success_criteria.failures: Premature submission, irrelevant recovery, stale answer, exhausted budget, invalid schema and transport errors remain distinct.
success_criteria.primary: More correct first proposals with actual decisive evidence recovery; no immediate-control regression.
success_criteria.status: Prospective design only; freeze fixtures, schedule, actual token exposure, independent oracle and attempt caps before dispatch.

records.falsifier: Under confirmed masking exposure, GLM fails to improve correct first proposals, selects irrelevant or stale evidence, submits prematurely, or exceeds its unchanged budget.
records.mechanism: The model can notice absent task evidence and select its recorded archive source when the tool remains offered; this behavior is not guaranteed by the gate or the scripted H19 result.
records.scope: Prospective model-behavior hypothesis only. Dense real-token recycling and ordinary masking require separately attributed exposure; no live H20 evidence exists.
records.statement: When a previously delivered decisive document fact is masked, GLM will use optional bounded archive recovery to improve first-proposal correctness compared with the forced-submission baseline.
